previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was readmitted six days after a prior discharge due to recurrent fevers, right upper quadrant pain, and nausea while on outpatient ertapenem for presumed cholangitis. Despite negative blood and urine cultures and no evidence of biliary obstruction on imaging, she was treated initially with meropenem and later daptomycin due to persistent fevers. After failing to respond to antibiotics and remaining afebrile off treatment, all antibiotics were discontinued. An ERCP showed chronic biliary narrowing consistent with PSC, and balloon dilation was performed. Diuretics were held initially but resumed when stable. She remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid antibiotics in the ED without consulting the liver team and to follow up for a repeat CT scan of a 5 mm lung nodule in one year.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with primary sclerosing 
cholangitis complicated by cirrhosis (Childs B) with ascites, 
hepatic encephalopathy, and varices and recent hospitalizations 
for cholangitis and FUO who presents with fevers, nausea, and 
abdominal pain.

#Fever of unknown origin: Pt has been admitted previously and 
been treated for cholangitis. During prior admission 
unremarkable MRCP, ERCP, CT, and negative culture. In the past 
has spiked fevers through both meropenem and daptomycin without 
clinical decompensation. During this admission patient had 
fevers to as high as 103. Antibiotics were not given. TTE 
negative for valvular lesions making culture negative 
endocarditis less likely. CRP and ESR elevated but nonspecific. 
RF was elevated at 112. Anti-CCP and cryocrit sent and pending 
at time of discharge. For malignancy w/u, CA ___ sent and will 
need colonoscopy as outpatient given quiescent UC for yearly 
surveillance. Patient did have mild bump in her liver tests 
during fever so unclear if rise was secondary to fever or 
possibly patient had mild biliary obstruction with cholangitis 
that cleared/opened up on its own. LFTs were normal at 
discharge.

# Primary sclerosing cholangitis w/ cirrhosis c/b ascites, HE 
and varices: 
- continued home lactulose and rifaximin. 
- continued home ursodiol and hydroxyzine.

-Patient should have colonoscopy in the following year
-Labs pending at time of discharge which should be followed up: 
anti-CCP, cryocrit and IFE
